message.content: {"B_expression":"-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)","C_expression":"-1/(sqrt(1+r)*(1+sqrt(1+r)))","derivation":"The correction is g = r/2 + chi_r*chi_u*(r^2*B + u*r*C). Setting u=0 and requiring g = sqrt(1+r)-1 exactly gives B = -1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2), the source-only formula. For u != 0 the residual with C=0 is E = 2*u*(sqrt(1+r)-1) + higher-order terms, which is O(u). Adding a C-term shifts g by u*r*C, changing E by 2*u*r*C*sqrt(1+r) + 2*u*(u*r*C) + ... Setting the O(u) coefficient to zero yields C = -1/(sqrt(1+r)*(1+sqrt(1+r))). With both B and C active, the residual reduces to E = -u^2*r/(1+r), which is O(u^2) and vanishes at u=0 and r=0. Both expressions are smooth for r > -1, which strictly contains the outer rectangle r in [-1/2, 1/2]. No interior zero of the radicand occurs. The chi factors smoothly suppress the correction outside the support, recovering g = r/2 there.","inspect":[{"file_id":"MATH_SOURCES/03_R3_EXACT_QUOTIENT.md","limit":2048,"offset":0}],"note":"B cancels the pure quadratic remainder exactly at u=0 within chi support; C removes the linear-in-u cross-term so the total residual is O(u^2). At subsequent stages where z != 1 (hence u != 0), the C-term is active. Both are smooth on an open neighborhood of the closed outer rectangle since 1+r >= 1/2 > 0. The source-only B alone is a valid degenerate choice (C=0) if one prefers the narrower scope. Outside the chi support the host falls back to g=r/2 regardless; this program does not alter that behavior. Certificate remains NOT_CERTIFIED: finite evaluation at sample points does not establish all-order smoothness of the composite with the C-infinity chi transitions, though the algebraic bodies themselves are manifestly C-infinity on the domain."}
